[member], that is an excellent question, and it deserves a properly sourced answer.

**Thesis:** In Legends, Darth Vader's feats place him among the most dangerous combatants of the Imperial era, in raw telekinesis and in lightsaber combat alike. Below are twelve of his strongest feats. Only Legends material is used; Canon material and image-only scans are excluded. Each entry gives one exact quote and its source.

**I. Telekinesis**

**1. Dismantling the Kachirho ramps to finish Roan Shryne**
- With his saber on his belt, Vader tears the wooden ramps apart and buries a veteran Jedi swordsman under the debris.
- "the floorboards were coming in larger and larger pieces, from all directions, and faster than he could parry them."
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 46

**2. Guiding a thrown lightsaber through a Jedi's telekinesis**
- Shryne tries to push the thrown blade off course and fails; it kills Fang Zar.
- "Calling on the Force, he tried to influence the course of the lightsaber, but either the Force wasn't with him or Vader's Force abilities were overpowering his."
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 34

**3. Breaking the Force shields of the Sa Cuis clones**
- Vader punches through the clones' Force shields and chokes several of them at once.
- "stabbed his Force reach through the shield of the Cuis clones, seizing their throats and crushing them."
- Source: Two-Edged Sword
-----CHUNK-----
**II. Power against top-tier opposition**

**4. Overpowering the enraged Starkiller clone**
- Vader throws aside the clone, which The Force Unleashed II calls more powerful than the original Galen Marek.
- "You grab your sabers and attack, but Vader is too powerful."
- Source: The Force Unleashed II: Prima Official Game Guide

**III. Lightsaber combat**

**5. Bol Chatak on Murkhana**
- Only weeks into the suit, clumsy and without a style of his own, Vader still takes Chatak's sword arm and then her head.
- "Vader had simply beaten her into submission"
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 11

**6. Siadem Forte and Iwo Kulka, two-on-one**
- Two skilled Knights using contrasting styles. Vader toys with them, beheads both together, and also cuts down three other Jedi.
- "Toying with the Jedi, he grazed Forte on the left shoulder, then on the right thigh"
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 41

**7. Roan Shryne, a thirty-year veteran swordsman**
- Shryne's only hits land on prosthetics. Once Vader presses with his grounded style, Shryne has no answer.
- "It was an old style, the very opposite of what was said to have been Dooku's style, and Shryne had no defense against it."
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 43

**8. Training duels with Galen Marek**
- An hours-long sparring session aboard the Executor in which his apprentice never scores a hit.
- "The fight had raged across the training deck of the Executor for hours, with Starkiller never landing a single blow, no matter how he tried."
- Source: The Force Unleashed II (novel)
- Scaling: Wookieepedia's Galen Marek article says Marek's later Death Star win came only through the Force. Without that advantage, it says, he would have been defeated and killed.
-----CHUNK-----
**IV. Force defense**

**9. Bare-handed blaster deflection (Tutaminis)**
- Holding his saber aside, Vader stops Shryne's repeated fire with his open hand.
- "Holding his lightsaber to one side, he raised his right hand to turn the blaster bolts."
- Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 33

**10. Halting I-Five's lasers (Force barrier)**
- The droid's lasers stop short of Vader's raised hand.
- "The beams sliced toward Vader . . . and stopped mere centimeters from his outstretched hand."
- Source: Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of the Force

**V. Durability**

**11. Surviving Mustafar**
- With no legs, one arm and burning flesh, he claws his way up the lava bank on hatred and the dark side.
- "Only his powers kept him from blacking out."
- Source: The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader

**VI. The decisive feat**

**12. Killing Darth Sidious**
- While the Emperor's lightning pours through his suit, Vader lifts him overhead and throws him down the reactor shaft.
- "He held the wailing despot high over his head, and with a final spasm of strength, hurled him into the abyss."
- Source: Return of the Jedi (prose adaptation)
- Scaling: Wookieepedia's Palpatine (Legends) article says many people, Vader and Luke included, considered Sidious the most powerful Sith Lord in history.
-----CHUNK-----
**Statements (not feats)**
These are claims about Vader, not demonstrations. They support the feats above but are not evidence on their own level.
- George Lucas, on Vader's power after Mustafar (an interview, not a Legends work): "So his ability to be twice as good as the Emperor disappeared, and now he’s maybe 20 percent less than him."
  Source: "Star Wars: The Last Battle," Vanity Fair, 2005
- Palpatine (as the guide's passage is attributed), on his apprentice: "Of all the monsters I have created, I still regard Darth Vader as something of a minor masterpiece."
  Source: Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (same passage: "the greatest Jedi killer of all time")
- Sidious, reassuring Vader after Mustafar: "There is none, my son, even though your body has been crippled."
  Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 19
- Bail Organa: "He's powerful almost beyond belief."
  Source: Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader, ch. 51

**Conclusion**
Even at his weakest, weeks after Mustafar, Vader beat Bol Chatak. By Kashyyyk he was dismantling several Jedi at once and overpowering a Knight's telekinesis. At the end of his life he killed the Emperor while being electrocuted. The statements add context, but the feats make the case.
